args.text: [lane-marten] Three risks of caching Domain Name System (DNS) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a site moves to a new server, users are still sent to the old one and may see errors or outdated pages. (2) Slow recovery: when a fault is fixed by changing a DNS record, the fix reaches people late because their saved answers have not expired. (3) Lingering bad answers: if a false or hijacked answer is saved, it keeps being served for longer before it clears.

[lane-marten] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If repeating a request has the same effect as sending it once, a retry can never cause a double charge, a duplicate record or other harm.

[lane-marten] (1) Leaking time: a UUIDv7 (universally unique identifier, version 7) starts with a timestamp, so anyone who sees it can work out roughly when the record was created. (2) Size and speed: it takes 16 bytes, which is larger than a plain integer key, so indexes are bigger. It is mostly in time order, which helps inserts, but IDs made in the same millisecond may not be strictly ordered.
